bet.text: A base designed around swerve modules as far out in the corners as possible, leaving the inside of the robot for a handoff and a wide intake.

demand.text: Watching a week 3 event moved a team member from two offense robots and one defender to three offense robots in strict lanes.
The team weighed a triple balance (10 points) against two hybrid cycles, a link and a park; balancing all three robots became the default.

auto.text: The Blooper launches the preloaded cube as soon as the match starts, so auto finishes a little faster.
Scripted sequences, team path planning and a gyro PID for balancing.
A forum table gives 1.5 auto pieces per championship qualification match.

cycle.text: The driver picks cone or cube mode. In cube mode a limit switch stops the intake rollers, closes the flippers and starts the handoff; flippers hold a cone in the same place for the arm, stowed near the middle of the robot.
A forum table gives 8.5 teleop pieces per championship qualification match.

endgame.text: Carbon fiber Forks go under an alliance partner, and a four-bar lifts and tilts the robot away from the floor.

fallback.text: With all three opponents balancing, the Swiper was meant to take cubes from their loading zone for quick cycles. The triple balance was the default, so the team used it perhaps once or twice in matches.

gave_up.text: L2 gearing, a slower speed in the team's words, helped keep a pretty tall robot steady; a ballast of about seven or eight pounds and a stainless belly pan were added against tipping.
A suction end effector kept weight low and handled both pieces on a prototype, but could not be packaged with a handoff of both from a separate floor intake.

changed.text: After the reveal: a lighter end effector, grout sponge rollers, L2 instead of L1 gears, a stronger belly pan and ballast. Red's frame bent during reveal filming, so the team set out to preserve and reinforce blue for the championships.
The Edgewalker was removed after Magnolia, because triple balancing proved far easier than expected; its space took the Swiper's vacuums.

outcome.text: 88-16-0 in official play; ranked 22 by championship OPR (69.58, Archimedes).

solves.text: Keep a tall robot steady and leave the inside free

facts.text: Square frame of custom sheet metal and billet; side
Swerve Drive Specialties Mk4 modules at L2, mounted "backwards" to increase the footprint
Superstructure of aluminum sheet, 1/16 in
A stainless steel ballast plate lowers the center of gravity
A bumper bracket has a lip over each module plate, because plates had bent near the mounting holes the year before

cost.text: The team calls L2 a slower speed, without saying slower than what

facts.text: Pivot ratio on a Falcon 500
Telescope ratio on a Falcon 500
Shimmed hex interfaces minimize backlash
Aluminum sheet of 0.040 in, carbon fiber telescope tubes and many Markforged printed parts

functions.name: Intake

solves.text: Pick up cones from multiple directions, and cubes without popping them

functions.type: vector roller and dustpan floor intake

facts.text: Grout sponge wheels, waterjet cut, run over a pool noodle roller; sponge sticks to cones and grabs cubes
Cones can enter from almost 180 degrees; the V-shaped roller brings the cone base to the back
Roller 6.25:1 on two Falcon 500s; pivot 60:1 on a Falcon 500
Flappers, 40:1 on a Falcon 500, center the cone and secure it through the handoff
A cone detection camera, plus a plunger limit switch that works only in cube mode
Bent polycarbonate takes impacts; waterjet sector gears deploy it

solves.text: Take cones and cubes from the floor intake by handoff

facts.text: Double rollers on one Falcon 500; dead-axle carbon fiber tubes save weight
Rollers are covered in high-temperature silicone tubing
White rollers take the cones and an open space takes the cubes
A simple reaction bar sits on the other end from the Everybot-style cone rollers, for cubes

solves.text: Score a preloaded cube at once in auto

facts.text: Adjustable extension spring and hard stop; servo-driven pin-puller release
Mostly 3D printed with carbon fiber rods; the release is a drone fishing payload release
100% accuracy stated for championship events

functions.name: Swiper

solves.text: Take cubes from the opponents' loading zone without extending outside the frame perimeter

functions.type: suction cups inside the frame perimeter

facts.text: Two suction cups in the bumper cutout, each with its own vacuum pump
Off-the-shelf pumps were refitted with legal 775 motors, whose speed must be held to the stock motor's, about 6000 rpm
Single-bellows cups held more firmly than double-bellows; vacuum-saving valves cut the holding force
A valve must vent the vacuum to release a light piece, as close to the cup as possible
Motor current drops and stays lower once a piece is held, which can be used to detect it
Built in about 24 to 36 hours (interview caption), three days (binder) or under four days (a team post)
The team's suction work found the vent valve must sit near the cup: on an arm, a valve on the chassis with tubing up the arm added around a second or two to release

solves.text: Lift and tilt the robot away from the floor, with rods that fit under an alliance partner

facts.text: Solid carbon fiber rods that fit under a partner; diameter 3/4 in
A non-parallel four-bar lifts and tilts the robot away from the floor
Lift 230:1 and fork deploy 28:1, each on a Falcon 500
Over-center deploy linkage, servo-released ratchet pawl and a camera for driver alignment

solves.text: Balance actively with two wheels hanging off the charge station

facts.text: Two rollers on two BAG motors worked with the two swerve modules on the station to move sideways along its edge
Removed after the Magnolia regional

cost.text: Not enough competitive advantage to keep improving once triple balancing proved far easier than expected

facts.text: Hex bolts are machined down, drilled and hex-broached, and thread into tapped hollow tubes of 1 in outside diameter and 1/8 in wall
Aluminum bolts are recommended over stainless for machinability
A hex shaft through the inside of the driving features keeps them from loosening
A 10-channel CAN board puts one device on each channel in a star topology
A power board feeds low-current devices, with four switchable channels, short-circuit, over-current and over-temperature protection and soft start
C++ with Lua-scripted autonomous and driver sequences, team swerve code and path planning
When locked on, the driver controls translation and vision tracking controls orientation
The gyro feeds a PID that balances on the charge station in auto

decisions.choice: Rollers with a reaction bar for cubes
decisions.because: suction on the arm could not be packaged with a handoff of both pieces from a floor intake
decisions.instead_of: a suction end effector, which kept weight low

decisions.because: it sticks to cones, grabs cubes without tearing and is durable
it helps keep the robot steady while it sprints across the field
decisions.cost: a slower speed, the team says (slower than what is not said); a team post says the robot moved from L1 to L2 after the reveal

decisions.choice: Add a suction Swiper between week 4 and week 5
decisions.because: cubes lay in the opponents' loading zone while all three opponents would be balancing
decisions.cost: used perhaps once or twice in matches

decisions.choice: Preserve the blue robot and reinforce its frame for the championship events
decisions.because: the red robot's frame was bent during reveal filming
